Witness: For D = (-1, 1) in dimension 1 with r = 1 and j(z) = 1/2 for |z| < 1, the formula yields 1/4 = 0.25, whereas the true principal eigenvalue is approximately 0.2245 < 0.25. In general, the formula equals the Rayleigh quotient of the constant function 1_D, which strictly exceeds the principal eigenvalue because the principal eigenfunction is non-constant on D (vanishing or decreasing towards the boundary). In the proof, Lemma 4.5 incorrectly applies Lemma 4.4 by confusing conditioning on the survival event up to time n with conditioning solely on S_n in D at step n (the quasi-stationary distribution is not the uniform distribution). Consequently, the formula in Theorem 2.1 is false in general. (Note that this also invalidates the claim in Theorem 2.3.)
